_provenance.note: District of Columbia citation authorities. DC's SNAP-specific policy is codified directly as STATUTE in DC Code Title 4, Chapter 2B ('Food Stamp Expansion Act'), cited by a section-number convention such as '4-261.02' (Categorical Eligibility for SNAP), plus a separate related section outside that chapter, '4-205.71' (drug-felon opt-out, in the TANF-focused Subchapter V of Chapter 2). This pack defines a 'dccode' citation family matching this format. Unlike Delaware's DSSM or many other states' agency-issued manuals, DC has NO dedicated DCMR (DC Municipal Regulations) chapter specifically for SNAP eligibility rules that this pack could locate — Title 29 DCMR ('Public Welfare') contains chapters for TANF, Medicaid, and other public-assistance programs but no chapter titled for food stamps/SNAP. This pack expects 'dccode' citations to dominate generated DC answers, distinct from the DCMR-section citation pattern most other built jurisdictions in this roster use.

patterns.note: DC Code Title 4 (Human Services), cited with its own section number, e.g. DC Code § 4-261.02 (Categorical Eligibility for SNAP), § 4-261.01 (Food Stamp Expansion Act definitions), § 4-261.03 (LIHEAP Heat and Eat initiative), § 4-261.21 (Transitional SNAP), § 4-205.71 (drug-felon opt-out for cash and food assistance).

Federal SNAP regulations (7 CFR Part 273 and related), used for figures DC's own materials state are federally set and subject to change each October 1 (income limits, resource limits, standard deduction, excess shelter cap, ABAWD time-limit rules), consistent with this roster's other blank-slate packs.

dccode.note: Food Stamp Expansion Act — Definitions (categorical eligibility, LIHEAP, Maximum Standard Utility Allowance, SNAP, TANF)

Categorical Eligibility for SNAP — grants categorical eligibility to all applicants at or below 200% FPL gross income via a Mayor-established TANF-funded program/service; originally enacted 3/3/2010, most recently amended 3/10/2023

LIHEAP Heat and Eat initiative — Mayor must provide maximum Standard Utility Allowance to all participants; automatic enrollment for SNAP households that would benefit from the $20.01 minimum annual LIHEAP benefit
Transitional SNAP — 5 months of transitional SNAP benefits after TANF cash assistance terminates due to a change in income, enacted as part of the SNAP Expansion Act of 2010 (D.C. Law 18-223)

Granting cash and food assistance benefits to drug felons — full, unconditional opt-out from the federal drug-felony SNAP/TANF ban; added 4/20/1999 (D.C. Law 12-241), amended 11/26/2019 (D.C. Law 23-31)

cfr.note: Resource eligibility standards — current federal floor $3,000 general / $4,500 elderly-disabled, matching DC's own DHS-stated current figures exactly (unlike this roster's Delaware pack, where DSSM 9045's own text was found stale/below this floor)
Benefit-amount calculation — net income x 0.3 subtracted from the household's maximum allotment, per DC DHS's own SNAP Monthly Benefit page description
ABAWD work requirement and time-limit rules — 3 countable months in a 3-year period; DC's own 36-month fixed clock (6/1/2026-5/31/2029) implements this at the District level
